Subject: Post-call recap: Lumenix reserved GPU fit assessment & next steps

Hi Alicia —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our end so we have alignment and clear next steps. Please flag anything we missed.

What we heard (pain & goals)
- Latency & predictability: P99 latency spikes during large-batch inference are causing timeouts in your ingestion pipeline. Goal: ~p99 <= 220ms for 2k token sequences under peak.
- Cost discipline: current spend on GPU inference is unpredictable; you want a predictable reserved commitment model to lower unit cost.
- Data isolation / compliance: PHI in payloads — wants tenant isolation or dedicated pool for regulated workloads plus audit logs (retention 12 months).
- Scale profile: baseline ~120 requests/s (RL), projected peak 300–350 requests/s for new model rollout; average sequence length ~1.6k tokens, bursts up to 6k tokens.
- Timeline: target pilot (production-readiness) in Q3 2026; procurement/PS cycle runs in parallel.

Proposed fit (high level)
- Dedicated reserved pool: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs in an isolated lane for PHI workloads with autoscale burst to 6 GPUs for short windows.
- SLOs: commercial scope: target 99.9% availability for control-plane, p99 inference latency target 220ms (can propose 99.95% with price uplift).
- Ops: canary rollout with 5% traffic, automatic fallback to non-isolated model if capacity constrained; prefix/KV caching for leading prompts to reduce token cost.
- Security: Redwood Private option (VPC) and KMS integration + SOC2 evidence.

Requested items from Lumenix (to size and finalize commercial):
1) Confirmation of monthly token volume (or monthly request count) and retention period for logs.
2) Any hard compliance requirements beyond HIPAA (e.g., HITRUST, FedRAMP).
3) Network & egress constraints; we'll need a short allowlist to size ingress NAT/bandwidth.
4) Preferred procurement cadence and PO contacts (procurement@...).

Attachments: lumenix_capacity_outline.xlsx (sizing & cost sketch), sla-draft.pdf (initial SLO language)

Next steps (owner / timeline)
- Alicia: confirm traffic profile and procurement contact by EOW (6/19).
- Ben: schedule technical runbook call to validate model memory and KV cache approach (we suggested 6/18 or 6/19).
- Marissa: share draft commercial term for reserved pool once traffic numbers confirmed.

If that's all accurate I'll queue Ben and Marissa to the technical runbook and draft. Thanks again — we think a reserved + burst lane with isolation is the cleanest path to hit the latency & compliance goals.

Appreciate the details, Alicia — that's exactly what we needed. Quick follow-up and a concrete sizing suggestion for internal review:

Sizing suggestion (preliminary)
- Baseline reserved pool: 4x H100-equivalent GPUs in an isolated lane for PHI workloads. This supports sustained ~200–300 reqs/s for 2k-token sequences with KV cache efficiency.
- Burst capacity: allow automatic short-term scaling to +2 GPUs (6 total) for traffic spikes to ~500 reqs/s using burst credits.
- Cache: enable prefix caching for the most common prompts (we estimate 18–25% token savings).
- Failover: route non-PHI to a shared hosted model if dedicated pool is saturated (policy-based routing).

SLA delta summary (ballpark)
- 99.9% availability: lower monthly commitment and smaller margin for burst — price estimate included in the attached worksheet.
- 99.95% availability: requires higher reserved headroom and a small premium (~8–12% on top of base reserved cost) to guarantee p99 targets during peaks. We'll have Ben provide the ops assumptions.

Let's get the technical runbook scheduled — Ben, can you take the lead for the technical deep-dive and confirm the checklist (model variant, KV cache, tokenization, network requirements)? Alicia, Ben proposed 30–45 minutes; he has availability tomorrow 6/18 10:00–11:00 PT or Friday 6/19 09:00–11:30 PT. Link: https://cal.com/ben-carter/lumenix-technical-runbook

I'll have Marissa prepare a short commercial note after we confirm traffic numbers.

Sergio
